newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Bangladeshi trade urges lifting of wheat subsidy.
newsitem.headline: Bangladeshi trade urges lifting of wheat subsidy.

text.p: Private Bangladesh grain traders urged their government on Friday to lift its subsidy on wheat, saying they were suffering from unfair competition with the government.
"We are suffering. That's why we're talking 'no more subsidies'," Syed M. Altaf Hussain of W&W Grains Corporation told Reuters at a wheat conference in Singapore. "It's a big problem (for us)."
Other dealers nodded their heads in agreement.
"The subsidy is killing us," one said.

Senior Bangladesh Food Ministry official Mohammad Abdur told the conference the subsidies would be "gradually reduced" but were are currently needed to prevent any sharp increase in the price of wheat products.
Hussain said the government releases an estimated 500,000 tonnes of wheat into the market each year. The wheat comes mainly from concessional programmes like food aid supplied by other countries.
The European Union alone supplies about 150,000 tonnes of wheat a year. The wheat enjoys a 30 percent subsidy from the government.
Hussain said private traders could not compete with the government unless the subsidy was lifted.

Analysts estimate Bangladesh will import about 1.6 million tonnes of wheat in fiscal 1997/98 beginning July. Some 700,000 tonnes will come in from food aid. Rice is the staple food for Bangladesh's 110 million people.
